html:
Red Vienna is the name for the city of Vienna from 1919 to 1934, when it was governed by the Social Democrats and built an ambitious programme of public housing and welfare.

After the fall of the Habsburgs, Vienna was the oversized capital of a small republic. The city council taxed luxuries and built about 64,000 flats in large courtyard blocks, such as the Karl Marx Hof, with laundries, kindergartens and clinics. It also expanded schools and health care.

The conservative federal government saw Vienna as a threat. In February 1934 a brief civil war ended with the army shelling the workers' housing blocks, and the Social Democratic party was banned under the dictatorship that ruled until the Anschluss. The city still owns a large share of housing, often cited as a model. Compare the Swedish welfare model. See Austria.
sum: Red Vienna is the name for the city of Vienna from 1919 to 1934, when it was governed by the Social Democrats and built an ambitious programme of public housing and welfare.
